description: To Sync your Ideas with Us
summary: TERRA-X is a Planetary Analogue Intelligence System that identifies and analyzes Earth environments resembling the terrain and environmental conditions of the Moon and Mars using scientific datasets. It helps researchers explore potential analogue sites, compare planetary characteristics, and evaluate mission suitability through interactive maps, data visualization, and intelligent similarity analysis.
details:
What it does and how it works

AnalogFinder is an interactive web tool that searches the whole Earth for places that resemble the Moon and Mars. Instead of picking one site because it looks similar, we turn the question into a measurable one. We describe a target (Moon South Pole, Mars Jezero, or Mars Gale) as a numeric profile built from space-agency data. We describe each Earth candidate site with the same features from NASA Earth observations. We then compute a weighted similarity score across six dimensions: terrain, temperature, geology, ice and water, dust, and subsurface.

Users see the results on an interactive world map, with markers colored from low to high match. They can adjust weight sliders to reflect their mission priorities, and the map re-scores instantly. Selecting a site opens a report with a radar chart, an explanation of why it matches, where the analogy breaks down, and how the site could be used for exploration. A “Hidden Gems” mode excludes well-known analog sites so that overlooked locations surface.

Benefits

It gives mission planners a systematic, data-driven way to find and compare analog sites instead of relying on a few well-known locations.
Weighting lets different missions (rover mobility, resource extraction, habitat construction, instrument testing) find the analog that fits their needs.
Each site report states its limits clearly, which supports honest scientific use.

Intended impact

We want to widen the set of Earth sites considered for lunar and Mars preparation, make it easier to find lower-cost and more accessible testing locations, and help the public understand that no Earth site is a perfect analog, but many can be useful for specific purposes. The method is reproducible, so it can be extended to a global grid search and to more targets.

Tools, languages, and software

Data: NASA and open datasets including [SRTM / Copernicus DEM, MODIS, SMAP, MERRA-2, LRO LOLA, LRO Diviner, MGS MOLA, USGS Astrogeology: list only what you actually used]
Languages and libraries: [Python (pandas, NumPy) for feature normalization and scoring; JavaScript, Leaflet, and Chart.js for the map and charts]
Design: Google Stitch for UI design [and the tool you used to build the working app]
Hosting and documentation: [GitHub, deployment platform]

How the project is creative

It is a method, not a single-site answer. Anyone can rerun it with new data or new targets.
It looks beyond visual similarity by combining multiple datasets into one comparable score.
The “Hidden Gems” filter deliberately excludes famous sites to find unrecognized analogs, including sites in places like India [confirm against your final results].
Interactive weighting lets users define what “analogous” means for their own mission.
Every result includes a “where the analogy breaks down” section, so the tool shows its limits rather than hiding them.

Factors our team considered

Analogy is dimension-specific. A site can be an excellent terrain analog but a poor temperature analog, so we score each dimension separately.
Earth cannot reproduce reduced gravity (0.166 g on the Moon, 0.38 g on Mars), vacuum or a thin atmosphere, or the radiation environment. We state this in every site report.
Scale matters. A specific crater or valley can match better than a whole desert, so we scored individual sites rather than whole regions.
Data quality and resolution differ across datasets, so we normalized features before comparing them.
Usability for mission planners, including clear visuals, adjustable priorities, and a side-by-side comparison mode.
